method: Independent AI semantic review of only each original unit's returned FIDs in its allowed same-claim evidence scope. Full parent claim resolves what a conjunction or referent asserts; it does not supply missing source proof. Named leading scope, identities, attributes, quantities, operations, conditions, purpose and direction are assessed without background equivalence, unselected neighboring text, cross-claim/sibling borrowing, or claim citation-union rescue.
claim_counting_rule: A claim is complete only when every original unit is complete with its own selected sources. Partial retains some core support but misses an asserted relation/identity/qualifier/attribute/purpose; unsupported has no adequate core support. Invalid structure would have no quality denominator.

comparison_with_actual43.interpretation: No complete source-selection success. Both export units now select the F020 continuation but lack its F019 subject/predicate bridge. Source completeness is evaluated on the full original unit, not an attribute-only or purpose-keyword denominator.

F001.exact_text: One of the G3P molecules leaves the Calvin cycle to contribute to the formation of the carbohydrate molecule, which is commonly glucose (C6H12O6).

F002.exact_text: Because the carbohydrate molecule has six carbon atoms, it takes six turns of the Calvin cycle to make one carbohydrate molecule (one for each carbon dioxide molecule fixed).

F003.exact_text: The remaining G3P molecules regenerate RuBP, which enables the system to prepare for the carbon-fixation step.

F004.exact_text: ATP is also used in the regeneration of RuBP.

F009.exact_text: Stage 3: Regeneration Interestingly, at this point, only one of the G3P molecules leaves the Calvin cycle and is sent to the cytoplasm to contribute to the formation of other compounds needed by the plant.

F011.exact_text: chloroplast has three carbon atoms, it takes three “turns” of the Calvin cycle to fix enough net carbon to export one G3P.

F012.exact_text: But each turn makes two G3Ps, thus three turns make six G3Ps.

F013.exact_text: One is exported while the remaining five G3P molecules remain in the cycle and are used to regenerate RuBP, which enables the system to prepare for more CO2 to be fixed.

F018.exact_text: The resulting six-carbon compound is broken down into two three-carbon compounds, and the energy in ATP and NADPH is used to convert these molecules into G3P.

F021.exact_text: The remaining G3P molecules stay in the cycle to be formed back into RuBP, which is ready to react with more CO2.

F056.exact_text: RuBisCO catalyzes a reaction between CO2 and RuBP, which forms a six-carbon compound that is immediately converted into two three-carbon compounds.

F057.exact_text: This process is called carbon fixation, because CO2 is “fixed” from its inorganic form into organic molecules.

F058.exact_text: ATP and NADPH use their stored energy to convert the three-carbon compound, 3-PGA, into another three-carbon compound called G3P.

F059.exact_text: This type of reaction is called a reduction reaction, because it involves the gain of electrons.

F064.exact_text: Stage 1: Fixation In the stroma, in addition to CO2, two other components are present to initiate the light-independent reactions: an enzyme called ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (RuBisCO), and three molecules of ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP), as shown in Figure 8.19.

F065.exact_text: RuBP has five atoms of carbon, flanked by two phosphates.
